title: Spain’s PM visits Ceuta after 57 migrants die breaching border from Morocco
facts: At least 57 migrants died while attempting to enter the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco.
Juan Jesus Vivas serves as the regional president of Ceuta.
Approximately 60,000 people crossed from Morocco into Ceuta within a 24-hour period.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez visited Ceuta following the border crossings.
Spain's Ministry of Interior reported that 25,000 migrants were returned from Ceuta to Morocco on Friday.
Rachid Sbihi leads a local Civil Guard workers' association in Ceuta.
Multiple migrants drowned or died in a stampede at Tarajal beach along the Ceuta border.
Ceuta and Melilla constitute the European Union's only terrestrial borders on the African continent.
Migrants frequently swim to Ceuta from the Moroccan coastal towns of Fnideq and Belyounech.
A Spanish Supreme Court ruling prohibited immediate returns of maritime migrant arrivals without due process.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for immediate cessation of unauthorized border crossings.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expressed support for Spain's border containment actions.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced reinforced border inspection controls along the French-Spanish border.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni threatened suspension of Schengen open-border arrangements with Spain.
Spain's Ministry of the Interior declined regional requests to declare a national state of emergency in Ceuta.
